title: The coffee test
setting: An afternoon in the office break area. Tanaka-san, Yuki and Mai's manager, stops by with news about the office coffee. Yuki mutters her first reaction to Mai, and Tanaka-san overhears the rest.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: yuki-san, kimura-san, chotto ii desu ka? raishuu kara, uchi no koohii ga yasui no ni kawarimasu.
lines.ja: ユキさん、木村さん、ちょっといいですか？来週から、うちのコーヒーが安いのに変わります。
lines.kana: ゆきさん、きむらさん、ちょっといいですか？らいしゅうから、うちのこーひーがやすいのにかわります。
lines.english: Yuki, Kimura-san, have you got a minute? From next week, the office coffee is switching to a cheaper one.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ima, chotto okane ga tarinai n desu. sumimasen ne.
lines.ja: 今、ちょっとお金が足りないんです。すみませんね。
lines.kana: いま、ちょっとおかねがたりないんです。すみませんね。
lines.english: Money's a bit tight right now. Sorry about that.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nani sore, imi wakannai. koohii gurai, ii jan.
lines.ja: 何それ、意味分かんない。コーヒーぐらい、いいじゃん。
lines.kana: なにそれ、いみわかんない。こーひーぐらい、いいじゃん。
lines.english: What? That makes no sense. Come on, it's only coffee.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kimochi wa wakaru kedo, watashi, koohii no chigai, yoku wakannai shi.
lines.ja: 気持ちは分かるけど、私、コーヒーの違い、よく分かんないし。
lines.kana: きもちはわかるけど、わたし、こーひーのちがい、よくわかんないし。
lines.english: I get how you feel, but I can't really tell one coffee from another anyway.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ee, watashi wa sugu wakaru yo. kesa no koohii mo, sugoku ii nioi shita mon.
lines.ja: えー、私はすぐ分かるよ。今朝のコーヒーも、すごくいい匂いしたもん。
lines.kana: えー、わたしはすぐわかるよ。けさのこーひーも、すごくいいにおいしたもん。
lines.english: Oh, come on, I can tell right away. This morning's coffee smelled amazing too.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: hee, yuki-san wa chigai ga wakaru n desu ne.
lines.ja: へえ、ユキさんは違いが分かるんですね。
lines.kana: へえ、ゆきさんはちがいがわかるんですね。
lines.english: Oh? So you can tell the difference, Yuki.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: はい！毎日飲んでますから。
lines.kana: はい！まいにちのんでますから。
lines.english: Yes! I drink it every day.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: demo, kesa no koohii wa, mou yasui no datta n desu yo.
lines.ja: でも、今朝のコーヒーは、もう安いのだったんですよ。
lines.kana: でも、けさのこーひーは、もうやすいのだったんですよ。
lines.english: But this morning's coffee was already the cheap one, you know.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? sumimasen, chotto imi ga yoku wakaranai n desu kedo.
lines.ja: え？すみません、ちょっと意味がよく分からないんですけど。
lines.kana: え？すみません、ちょっといみがよくわからないんですけど。
lines.english: Huh? Sorry, I don't quite follow.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kesa, yasui no de tsukutte mita n desu. dare ka ki ga tsuku kana to omotte.
lines.ja: 今朝、安いので作ってみたんです。誰か気がつくかなと思って。
lines.kana: けさ、やすいのでつくってみたんです。だれかきがつくかなとおもって。
lines.english: I tried making it with the cheap one this morning. I wanted to see if anyone would notice.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, honto desu ka? zenzen chigai ga wakarimasen deshita.
lines.ja: えっ、ほんとですか？全然違いが分かりませんでした。
lines.kana: えっ、ほんとですか？ぜんぜんちがいがわかりませんでした。
lines.english: What, really? I couldn't tell the difference at all.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: yuki, sugu wakaru tte itteta yo ne.
lines.ja: ユキ、すぐ分かるって言ってたよね。
lines.kana: ゆき、すぐわかるっていってたよね。
lines.english: Yuki, you said you could tell right away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. demo, imi wakannai. sugoku ii nioi shita noni.
lines.ja: うん。でも、意味分かんない。すごくいい匂いしたのに。
lines.kana: うん。でも、いみわかんない。すごくいいにおいしたのに。
lines.english: Yeah. But it makes no sense. It smelled so good.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sono kimochi, yoku wakarimasu yo. watashi mo senshuu nonde mite, zenzen chigai ga wakaranakatta n desu.
lines.ja: その気持ち、よく分かりますよ。私も先週飲んでみて、全然違いが分からなかったんです。
lines.kana: そのきもち、よくわかりますよ。わたしもせんしゅうのんでみて、ぜんぜんちがいがわからなかったんです。
lines.english: I know exactly how you feel. I tried it last week, and I couldn't tell the difference at all either.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.kana: え、たなかさんもですか？

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: hai. dakara, takai no ni shite mo imi ga nai n desu yo.
lines.ja: はい。だから、高いのにしても意味がないんですよ。
lines.kana: はい。だから、たかいのにしてもいみがないんですよ。
lines.english: Yes. So there's no point going with the expensive one.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: wakarimashita. yasui no de daijoubu desu.
lines.ja: 分かりました。安いので大丈夫です。
lines.kana: わかりました。やすいのでだいじょうぶです。

choices.english: Yuki spots the cheap coffee right away, so Tanaka-san keeps the old coffee.
The coffee Yuki praised was already the cheap one, so she accepts the change.
Mai can't tell the coffees apart, so Tanaka-san asks Yuki to pick the new one.

questions.explanation: Lines 1 and 3: Tanaka-san says the office coffee will switch to a cheaper one from next week because money is tight. Line 6: Yuki says she can tell right away, and that this morning's coffee smelled amazing. Line 9: Tanaka-san says this morning's coffee was already the cheap one, and in line 11 he explains he made it that way to see if anyone would notice. Line 12: Yuki couldn't tell the difference at all, and in line 18 she says the cheap one is fine. A is wrong: Yuki didn't notice the cheap coffee (line 12), and Tanaka-san goes ahead with it (line 17). C is wrong: Mai does say she can't really tell coffees apart (line 5), but nobody is asked to choose anything. Tanaka-san had already made up his mind.

questions.english: When Tanaka-san explains why the coffee is changing, what does Yuki mutter to Mai?
questions.ja: コーヒーが変わると聞いて、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: こーひーがかわるときいて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: koohii ga kawaru to kiite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: What? I don't know the meaning.

questions.explanation: Line 4: 'nani sore, imi wakannai.' imi wakannai (with ga dropped) means the meaning doesn't get through to her: cutting back on coffee makes no sense to her. She says it again in line 14, when she can't work out how the cheap coffee smelled so good. In line 10 Mai uses the polite version (chotto imi ga yoku wakaranai n desu kedo), because 'from next week' and 'already this morning' don't add up. B is wrong: imi nai means 'it's pointless'. That's what Tanaka-san says at the end (line 17: takai no ni shite mo imi ga nai), and it's a different idea. A is wrong: shiru is for knowing a fact, so imi shiranai sounds as if she has never learned what a word means. Getting what something means takes wakaru.

questions.english: It's Sunday evening, and Yuki sighs, "aa, ashita shigoto ka. iya da naa." (Ugh, work tomorrow. I don't want to go.) Tell her you know just how she feels.
questions.ja: あー、明日仕事か。いやだなあ。
questions.kana: あー、あしたしごとか。いやだなあ。
questions.romaji: aa, ashita shigoto ka. iya da naa.
questions.answer: Show that you relate with kimochi and wakaru, dropping ga in casual speech: wakaru wakaru, sono kimochi, or sono kimochi, sugoku wakaru. Don't use kimochi o shitteru.

modelAnswers.ja: 分かる分かる、その気持ち。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, I totally know how you feel.

modelAnswers.romaji: sono kimochi, sugoku wakaru. watashi mo ashita shigoto da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: その気持ち、すごく分かる。私も明日仕事だよ。
modelAnswers.english: I know exactly how you feel. I've got work tomorrow too.

questions.explanation: In line 15 Tanaka-san says 'sono kimochi, yoku wakarimasu yo' when Yuki can't believe she missed the cheap coffee. That's plain sympathy, which is what you want here. In line 5 Mai says 'kimochi wa wakaru kedo', with wa and kedo. That version leads into a 'but' (I get it, but...), so it's for disagreeing gently and doesn't fit when you simply feel for someone. Don't say kimochi o shitteru: shiru is for knowing a fact, so it sounds like you've found out what her feelings are, a bit like discovering a secret crush. Yuki speaks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Sora works at a café. He hands you two cups and says, "kore ga takai koohii de, kore ga yasui no. nonde mite. dou?" (This one's the expensive coffee, and this one's the cheap one. Try them. Well?) Tell him whether you can tell the difference.
questions.ja: これが高いコーヒーで、これが安いの。飲んでみて。どう？
questions.kana: これがたかいこーひーで、これがやすいの。のんでみて。どう？
questions.romaji: kore ga takai koohii de, kore ga yasui no. nonde mite. dou?
questions.answer: Use chigai with wakaru, dropping ga in casual speech: zenzen chigai wakannai if you can't tell them apart, or chigai wakaru yo if you can. Answer casually, since Sora speaks casually.

modelAnswers.ja: うーん、全然違い分かんない。
modelAnswers.english: Hmm, I can't tell the difference at all.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, chigai wakaru yo. takai no, sugoku ii nioi suru.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、違い分かるよ。高いの、すごくいい匂いする。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I can tell the difference. The expensive one smells really good.

questions.explanation: In the scene Mai says she can't really tell coffees apart (line 5: koohii no chigai, yoku wakannai), and Tanaka-san teases Yuki with 'chigai ga wakaru n desu ne' (line 7). Then Yuki and Tanaka-san both admit they couldn't tell at all: 'zenzen chigai ga wakarimasen deshita' (line 12) and 'zenzen chigai ga wakaranakatta' (line 15). wakaru takes ga, or no particle in casual speech, never o, so chigai o wakaranai is wrong. 'Tell' here isn't iu or oshieru: chigai o oshiete would ask Sora to explain the difference. zenzen means 'not at all' only with a negative.

newWords.english: expensive (also 'tall', as in se ga takai)
